quote: I'm just calling because we got that solar estimate built for your home. Just haven't been able to get it out to you yet. So I just need to find a good time for our specialist to bring that over.
stewart_read: The rep skips company/state framing and any reference to how the estimate was requested, moving straight to scheduling logistics. This works here because the customer doesn't push back, but it leaves no legitimacy anchor if he had been more skeptical.
alternative_hypothesis: Strategic compression given the customer immediately engages with scheduling questions rather than suspicion, so the omission cost nothing on this particular call.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to keep a one-line legitimacy anchor (source of the estimate/lead) even when leading with 'we already built this for you' — it's a habit that will fail on a more skeptical customer.

quote: You just need to pay income tax and have a credit score above six fifty. Is that the case for you?
stewart_read: The schema's stated credit threshold is 670; this rep states 650, the same drift previously documented in SESSION18_fcbf33c1. This is a schema_drift_detection flag — either the rep is wrong or floor policy has quietly shifted, and it needs reconciliation rather than being treated as a one-off rep error.
coaching_implication: Flag to management: confirm the active threshold with Kenny. If 650 is now correct, the schema needs updating; if 670 is correct, this rep (and possibly others) needs correction on the qualifier language.

quote: Which house did you do it for? The 26,170 or the 26474?
stewart_read: Customer volunteers that he owns two properties and needs to confirm which address the estimate was built for. This is a legitimate address-verification moment, not a scam-suspicion or time-constraint objection, so it doesn't cleanly map to an existing protocol in the schema.
coaching_implication: No coaching correction needed on the rep's handling (he confirmed the correct address: 'It's the 26170'), but note this as an unmapped scenario — multi-property customers may need a documented verify step for address confirmation.

quote: I'm I'm real busy right now.
stewart_read: The customer explicitly signals time pressure while the rep is mid-lookup ('Yeah. Let me go look real quick what we have.'). The rep does not acknowledge the busy signal verbally before continuing the process, which risks the customer disengaging mid-call.
alternative_hypothesis: Reactive gap — the rep was mid-task (checking calendar) and likely didn't have a natural pause to acknowledge; this is a minor miss rather than a pattern of dismissiveness.
coaching_implication: Small coaching note: a quick 'I know you're busy, I'll be fast' would have kept the customer's goodwill higher going into the logistics collapse that follows seconds later.

quote: My scheduler is not here right now, and my computer is not working.
stewart_read: This is the pivotal moment the call needed a firm recovery move — instead the rep accepts an open-ended 'call after 3PM tomorrow' with no confirmed day/time for the actual appointment, and no 'is that fair?' handshake.
alternative_hypothesis: Strategic accommodation — given the customer's stated real obstacles (no computer, no scheduler), forcing a lock-in here could have felt pushy; deferring to text/callback may have been the more customer-respectful move.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to still anchor a specific callback window ('I'll call you tomorrow at 3:15') rather than the vaguer 'call me after 3PM' — even a soft callback needs a rep-owned specific time to protect show/contact rate.

quote: Okay. It looks like it'd be easier for us to do a phone call. So the phone call would be just forty minutes long. We would just go over everything.
stewart_read: Rep does specify the channel (phone) and duration (forty minutes) proactively, which is a partial button-up even though no date/time exists yet to attach it to.
coaching_implication: Positive habit to reinforce — the rep is thinking ahead to logistics framing even without a locked date, but this needs to be paired with an actual callback time to be complete.

quote: Does that sound good? I gotta go. I yeah. I gotta go. Yeah. Do that. Thank you. Yep. Take care.
stewart_read: The call ends on the customer's rushed exit with no verbal handshake ('is that fair?') and no specific reconfirmed time — the rep's closing line is cut off by the customer leaving the call.
coaching_implication: Even in a rushed ending, the rep should get one locked specific — 'I'll text you today and call tomorrow at 3:15' — before letting the customer go, to leave a concrete artifact for the next touch.
